_comment: Shared parity fixture for the per-session figures the sessions list shows and filters on.
Two implementations compute them: session_query.go's SQL expressions, which the server
filters and sorts a page by, and frontend/src/lib/sessionMetrics.ts, which renders the
columns. They must agree exactly — a row displaying $36.30 must not be hidden by
'cost at most $40' — and before the filtering moved server-side that class of bug had
already happened once, which is why sessionMetrics.ts exists at all.
inserts each session and asserts the SQL, and frontend/src/lib/sessionMetrics.test.ts
asserts the TypeScript. Change a definition on one side and the other side's test fails,
rather than the two disagreeing in production.
Every figure but `messages` sums the main thread and its delegated sub-agents. `messages`
is deliberately main-thread only, matching the column beside it: message_count and
event_count are not rolled up, exactly as Usage and Cost are not.
`duration` is ACTIVE duration — inter-event gaps capped at the idle threshold — never the
start/last wall-clock span. A resumed-after-28-days session's span carried 82% of the
dashboard's average duration on its own.

cases.name: delegated work is added, never dropped
a session that delegated nothing contributes zero, not null
sub-agent time alone still counts as active duration
